comment.narrative: Mediumterm expenditure framework or other policy document for each entity envisages at least one reform to expand fiscal space for health

Fiscal space analysis was initiated to understand the potential of increasing and improving the financing of priority health expenditures. This activity seeks to assess fiscal space for health. Here fiscal space refers to the budgetary room allowing a government to provide resources for public purposes without impacting fiscal sustainability. Particularly the assessment focuses on five potential sources conducive macroeconomic conditions reprioritization of health within the government budget earmarked income and consumption taxes directed toward the health sector better efficiency of existing health expenditure and external aid. Given the current economic context it gives greater emphasis to domestic sources looking at both revenue and expenditure policy options and pays specific attention to improving the effectiveness and efficiency of public funds to make space for new health expenditures within the existing budget envelope. To this end data collection and analysis have commenced on 1 modeling the potential gains in health and revenue from increased excise taxation of tobacco alcohol and sugarsweetened beverages and 2 optimizing the efficiency of the health system and healthcare delivery.

Therefore progress towards these outcomes and MDTF objectives was adequate to the identification and initiation stage. Continued discussions with health authorities and service providers contributed to these outcomes by raising their awareness of key challenges and specific actions that need to be taken to ensure the provision of quality citizencentric services and to strengthen public financial management in the health sector. Activities ongoing under Pillar 1 Strengthening PeopleCentered Primary Health Care Care cascade analysis of selected NCDs was launched in FBiH.Support to conducting the population health surveys using European Health Interview Survey EHIS as a basis was defined a priority by both entities. Support to the development of RS digital health strategy is underway. The project implementation was launched following the World Banks approval of the Projects Concept Note on May 31 2023. The AA with EC was signed on December 9 2022 and amended on November 10 2023 to reflect the ECs internal project end date of January 31 2027. The Amendment to the AA between the World Bank and the SDC to reflect the SDC contribution to the project was signed on November 10 2023. The SDCs internal project start date is February 1 2024 and its internal project end date is January 31 2027.
